requirements.evidence: The full contract is present and behaves as specified: migrations with the exact index names (database/migrations/2026_10_29_033008_create_entity_memberships_table.php:25-26; 2026_10_29_033007_create_entities_table.php:21), models/enum/relations (app/Models/Entity.php:48, app/Models/User.php:56), both policies (app/Policies/EntityPolicy.php:46, app/Policies/EntityMembershipPolicy.php:31-45), pick with audit log (app/Http/Controllers/EntityController.php:18-27), three authorized Livewire pages (app/Livewire/Entity/Settings.php:26-32, Members.php:27-32, Dashboard.php:17-21), routes (routes/web.php:26-31) and both locales. Edge cases are handled: duplicate member and invalid roles (Members.php:55-57, 77), last-manager and owner protection (Members.php:81, 98), foreign/absent ids (Members.php:124-128), and vanished owner row during transfer (Settings.php:88-95).

conventions.evidence: Follows the project patterns: policy-based authorization, #[Validate] plus rules() (Members.php:24, Settings.php:35-44), #[Fillable] attributes (Entity.php:14), generated-style migrations with reversible down(), Blade components (x-form-field, x-button), audit-channel logging, and docs/CHANGELOG updates. Deviations: entity/membership domain writes run inline in the Livewire components instead of app/Actions/* (Settings.php:46-105, Members.php:37-120); the same CHANGELOG entry is added a second time under the released section (CHANGELOG.md:39); targetMembershipId is client-writable but absent from rules() (Settings.php:24).

security.evidence: No weakness found. The bound entity is #[Locked] in every component (Dashboard.php:14, Members.php:21, Settings.php:17); every public action re-authorizes server-side (Members.php:39,74,93; Settings.php:48,62,81) and resolves client-supplied ids scoped to the entity (Members.php:124-128; Settings.php:83-95, including the admin-only target query at 92); role input is constrained with Rule::in (Members.php:77); email uses exists:users,email; all views escape with {{ }}; addMember is rate-limited (Members.php:41-49) and secrets/mass assignment are controlled.

tests.evidence: Eight new Pest files cover the schema invariants (EntityDataModelTest.php:59-105), policies (EntityPoliciesTest.php:20-108), pick/session/audit (EntityPickTest.php:27-65), dashboard (EntityDashboardTest.php), members and settings. Unauthorized calls (EntityMembersTest.php:87-99; EntitySettingsTest.php:19-33), tamper attempts on locked state and ids (EntityMembersTest.php:133-145, 208; EntitySettingsTest.php:98-108) and both locales are tested; no existing test was weakened or removed.

simplicity.evidence: Lean and direct: reuses Eloquent relations, local role scopes, policies and Rule::unique; a single small helper resolves membership ids (Members.php:122-128); transactions only where multi-row consistency is needed (Settings.php:64-67, 87-100). No service/repository layers or speculative abstractions were added. Only a small per-row policy-call inefficiency in the list view (members.blade.php:22,36) remains.

readability.evidence: Small, documented methods with clear names (Members.php:34-60, 70-107; Settings.php:35-105), consistent layout attributes and sibling style, explanatory comments only where the invariant is non-obvious (migration owner_seq, transfer demote-first). Only a dead variable in one test (EntityMembersTest.php:137).

scope.evidence: The diff is limited to the entity feature: migrations, models, enum, factories, policies, controller, Livewire components/views, routes, lang files and the related docs/CHANGELOG entries. The extras (rate limiting at Members.php:41-49, clearing the session on self-leave at Members.php:106-108) directly support the required security/edge-case behavior; there are no unrelated refactors or out-of-scope features (no onboarding, switcher page or middleware).

issues.explanation: The identical Entities entry is added both under [Unreleased] (line 12) and under the already released [0.0.0] - 2026-07-07 section, falsely attributing the feature to the old release.

Entity settings and membership changes are domain writes, yet they are implemented inline in the Livewire components instead of the project's one-class-per-use-case app/Actions/* pattern (conventions.md), which also hides the delete/transfer transactions from reuse and unit-level testing.

The client-writable targetMembershipId has no #[Validate] rule or rules() entry; it is guarded ad hoc with filter_var plus 403 in transfer() (Settings.php:83-95), which is safe but does not follow the mandatory validate-public-properties convention.
The entities block still lists locale_default even though the doc now declares entities as implemented and the migration creates no such column, leaving the schema doc inaccurate.
The $foreignOwnerOfBoth membership is created but never used or asserted, which is dead setup code in the test.
Each table row calls @can/@cannot for assignRole and delete, and each policy check re-queries membershipFor(), producing roughly two queries per member instead of caching the viewer's role once.

review.summary: The change implements the entities and entity_memberships schema, models, enum, factories and policies, the entity.pick endpoint and the owner-only Livewire dashboard, members and settings pages, with both locales, docs and a thorough Pest suite. It meets the functional contract and the Livewire security rules; the deductions are structural: domain writes live inline instead of in app/Actions, the CHANGELOG entry is duplicated in the released section, and targetMembershipId is missing from the validation rules. I could not verify repo assets referenced outside the diff (layout, ui.welcome key, audit channel), hence medium confidence.
